questions.prompt: Collet's 1770 map of North Carolina shows mountains as:
choices: Pictures of hills, with no heights
questions.explain: Pictorial relief shows where hills are, but not how high.

questions.prompt: Who joined points of equal height with lines to summarize the Schiehallion survey?
questions.explain: Hutton's lines, published in 1778, became contour lines.

questions.prompt: The 1774 Schiehallion survey was made to:
choices: Estimate the density of the Earth
questions.explain: Maskelyne measured how the mountain's mass pulled a plumb line sideways.

questions.prompt: On a topographic map, contour lines very close together mean:
questions.explain: Elevation changes quickly over a short distance.

questions.prompt: A thicker, labeled contour line every fourth or fifth line is:
questions.explain: Index contours carry the elevation labels.

questions.prompt: Where a contour line crosses a stream valley, it bends into a V that points:
questions.explain: Contours bend upstream.

questions.prompt: A digital elevation model is:
choices: A raster in which each cell holds one elevation
questions.explain: A grid of elevations, usually in meters above a vertical datum.

questions.prompt: U.S. DEMs usually give elevations relative to:
choices: The highest point in the DEM
questions.explain: NAVD 88 is close to mean sea level.

questions.prompt: The first global DEM, released by the USGS in 1996 with cells about 1 km across, was:
questions.explain: GTOPO30: 30 arc-seconds, about 1 km.

questions.prompt: The Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (2000) mapped elevation with:
questions.explain: Two radar antennas, one on a 60 m mast.

questions.prompt: Lidar measures distance by:
questions.explain: Light detection and ranging.

questions.prompt: A lidar first return over a forest usually comes from:
questions.explain: First returns build a DSM.

questions.prompt: Why can lidar map the ground under a forest when air photos can't?
choices: Some pulses pass through gaps in the canopy to the ground
questions.explain: Those ground returns build the bare-earth DEM.

questions.prompt: A surface that includes roofs, tree canopies, and power lines is a:
questions.explain: Digital surface model: the first surface hit.

questions.prompt: A bare-earth model with ridge lines and stream lines added as breaklines is a:
questions.explain: Digital terrain model.

questions.prompt: To model where floodwater will flow, use:
questions.explain: Water runs over the ground, not the treetops.

questions.prompt: To check whether buildings block a cell tower's signal, use:
questions.explain: Signals are blocked by whatever is on the surface.

questions.prompt: Free DEMs for the whole United States are downloaded from:
questions.explain: apps.nationalmap.gov/downloader.

questions.prompt: The 1/3 arc-second DEM has cells about how wide?
questions.explain: 1 arc-second ≈ 30 m, so 1/3 ≈ 10 m.

questions.prompt: You switch from a 30 m DEM to a 10 m DEM of the same area. About how many times as many cells does it have?
For a project in Peru, which free DEM is generally the best place to start?
questions.explain: It has fewer voids than SRTM or ASTER GDEM. Note that it is a DSM.

questions.prompt: A cell lower than all its neighbors, which traps modeled water, is a:
questions.explain: Remove sinks with the Fill tool before hydrology.

questions.prompt: NoData holes in a radar DEM over steep mountains are:
questions.explain: Fill them from another source before analysis.

questions.prompt: A slope map from a DEM in latitude and longitude shows almost every cell near 90°. The most likely cause is:
choices: x and y are in degrees but z is in meters
questions.explain: Project the DEM to meters, or set a z-factor.

questions.prompt: A z-factor:
choices: Converts z values to the units of x and y
Sets the vertical exaggeration of a map
Counts the cells in a DEM
questions.explain: Or project the DEM first.

questions.prompt: A slope of 45° is how many percent?
questions.explain: Rise equals run, so 1 × 100.

questions.prompt: Percent slope is:
questions.explain: It can be more than 100.

questions.prompt: Slope in degrees can be more than 90.
questions.explain: Degrees run from 0 to 90; percent has no upper limit.

questions.prompt: The method ArcGIS Pro's Slope tool uses, with all eight neighbors and double weight on the direct neighbors, is:
Fleming and Hoffer's method estimates slope from:
questions.explain: Left and right, up and down.

questions.prompt: With 50 m cells, the left neighbor is 95 and the right neighbor is 50. What is (right − left) ÷ 2D?
The same 3 × 3 window gives 27.2° by Fleming and Hoffer and 20.5° by Horn. What does this show?
choices: The method is part of the result
questions.explain: Horn averages more cells and is less sensitive to noise.

questions.prompt: Slope, aspect, and hillshade are which kind of raster function?
questions.explain: Each uses a 3 × 3 window.

questions.prompt: ArcGIS Pro's Hillshade tool outputs values from:
questions.explain: An 8-bit range.

questions.prompt: What is the default sun azimuth for a hillshade, in degrees?
questions.explain: The northwest.

questions.prompt: The sun's altitude is:
questions.explain: The default is 45°.

questions.prompt: A hillshade lit from the southeast makes many readers see valleys as ridges. This is:
questions.explain: Cartographers light from the upper left to avoid it.

questions.prompt: Which four angles determine a cell's brightness in a hillshade?
choices: Sun azimuth, sun altitude, cell slope, and cell aspect
Cell size, extent, slope, and NoData
questions.explain: The relative radiance equation.

questions.prompt: Putting a semi-transparent color DEM over a hillshade:
questions.explain: This is shaded relief, used on most basemaps.

questions.prompt: Aspect is:
choices: The compass direction a slope faces
questions.explain: Measured clockwise from north.

questions.prompt: A cell with an aspect of 180° faces:
questions.explain: 0 north, 90 east, 180 south, 270 west.

questions.prompt: A cell with an aspect of 90° faces:
questions.explain: Measured clockwise from north.

questions.prompt: In ArcGIS Pro, flat cells get an aspect of:
questions.explain: Flat cells have no downslope direction.

questions.prompt: In North Carolina, which slopes get the most sun?
questions.explain: In the Northern Hemisphere the sun is to the south.

questions.prompt: Why should an aspect map label each direction in its legend?
choices: The meaning is carried only by color, which not every reader can tell apart
Labels make the map load faster
questions.explain: So the map works for readers with color vision deficiency.

questions.prompt: A line-of-sight test asks:
choices: Whether one target is visible from one observer
Which areas a tower can see
questions.explain: Viewshed repeats it for every cell.

questions.prompt: In a line-of-sight test, if a point between the observer and the target has a higher elevation angle than the target, the target is not visible.
questions.explain: That point blocks the view.

questions.prompt: An observer at 50 m looks at a target 100 m away at 20 m. What is the target's elevation angle, in degrees, to one decimal?
A viewshed is:
choices: The area visible from one or more observer points
questions.explain: Line of sight to every cell.

questions.prompt: In ArcGIS Pro, an observer's height above the ground for a viewshed is set in the field:
questions.explain: For example 1.7 m for a person, or 30 m for a tower.

questions.prompt: A viewshed run on a bare-earth DEM shows what you could see:
choices: With no trees or buildings in the way
questions.explain: Use a DSM when obstructions matter.

questions.prompt: Over long distances, viewshed tools can correct for:
questions.explain: The Earth curves away by about 7 m at 10 km.

questions.prompt: Put these ways of showing elevation in the order they appeared.
questions.explain: 1770 Collet, 1774 Hutton, USGS from 1879, DEMs from the late 1950s.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of preparing a DEM for slope analysis in order.
answer: Download tiles from The National Map
questions.explain: Project before Slope so x, y, and z share units.
